title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1970-09-20
source: Source Info: Master Soundboard Reels (borrowed by Peter Kafer) > Will Boswell's reel @ 7 1/2 ips; Transfer Info: Reel (Technics RS1506) > Tascam DA-3000 (DSF 1bit/5.6 MHz) > dBpoweramp 24/96 > Adobe Audition 3.0 > TLH flac2496

ai_review.summary: Stunning soundboard capture of a superb 9/20/70 performance, highlighted by an epic “To Lay Me Down” with mournful TC piano and stellar fills from Jerry, David Nelson and David Grisman.
ai_review.review: Reviewers rave about the musical excellence of this September‑1970 show – Jerry’s solemn treatment of “To Lay Me Down,” soaring acoustic moments on “Cumberland Blues” and “New Speedway Boogie,” and complementary organ‑piano interplay. The soundboard recording is praised as crisp and vivid, with no reported technical flaws, making the set a must‑listen for Deadheads.

ai_rating.rationale: All five reviews are strongly positive (average 4.6★), highlighting both an outstanding performance and excellent soundboard quality.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with no noted drop‑outs or muffiness; reviewers describe the audio as stunning.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The concert blends acoustic and electric material smoothly, typical of the 1970 era, with strong transitions and a cohesive overall vibe.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His solemn, longing guitar work on “To Lay Me Down” is singled out as perfect.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s rhythm guitar/vocals are heard “doing his thing,” noted in a secondary review.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s soft, mournful piano is praised for complementing Pigpen’s organ; some listeners were surprised by the piano’s tone.
